text:
sam: hitting a weird TS/ESM issue with the starter sample in the edge runtime. Node + CJS works, but after our edge bundler step the types collapse to `any` and overloads vanish.

alex: ugh. can you share a tiny repro or the failing error?

sam: yes — simplified: 
```ts
// src/index.ts
export function send(x: string): string;
export function send<T>(x: T): T;
export function send(x: any) { return x }
```
importing from the ESM build in an edge app shows `send` as `any` in editor and runtime types feel wrong. no TS errors during build.

maria: do you have package.json exports/entries? edge bundlers sometimes prefer the `module`/`.mjs` path which can point to a file that has no d.ts or a different generated d.ts.

sam: package.json: 
```json
{"main":"dist/index.cjs","module":"dist/index.mjs","types":"dist/index.d.ts","exports":{"import":"./dist/index.mjs","require":"./dist/index.cjs"}}
```
but dist/index.d.ts exists and has the overloads.

lee: another gotcha: our ts build emits `export =`/interop shims depending on `module` target. Also `tsup`/`esbuild` can strip generics in declaration emit if config mismatches. are you using `declarationMap` or `preserveSymlinks`?

alex: quick checklist i've used:
- ensure tsconfig `moduleResolution` is `node` or `bundler` consistently across build and IDE
- confirm `declaration` true + single `types` entry that points to the ESM entry (not just cjs)
- if you have conditional exports, add `typesVersions` or duplicate `index.d.ts` for both paths
- as temporary workaround, `skipLibCheck: true` hides the noise but not ideal

maria: also watch for `unknown` vs `any` leak: if one overload uses `unknown` and the implementation uses `any`, TS may widen the surface when the d.ts is post-processed. the bundler sometimes rewrites imports to runtime helpers that lose generic constraints.

sam: thanks — i tried pointing `types` at `dist/index.mjs.d.ts` and that made editor happier. still want to understand root cause.

lee: maybe we should change our starter sample build to emit unified `dist/esm/index.mjs` + `dist/types/index.d.ts` and add a tiny postbuild step that copies types into both export subpaths. reduces edge surprises.

sam: created a PR with changes and a minimal failing test (link: https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk/pull/1732) :tada:

alex: nice. can we also add a short troubleshooting note to the starter README explaining `module` vs `moduleResolution` and the `types` gotcha? saved me several times. :eyes:

dev-bot: created issue #458: "starter: ESM/CJS typing mismatch in edge starter sample" and linked PR 1732.

maria: assigning to eng-devex to review build changes. if we adopt postbuild copy, let's add a tiny script and mention performance tradeoffs in comments.

sam: will follow up tomorrow with CI failure logs if any. thanks all for rapid suggestions. :slightly_smiling_face:
